chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hisham ibn Salim from Muhammad ibn Muslim said:
Abu Basir prayed behind us on the road to Mecca, and he said while he was in prostration, and a she-camel of theirs had been lost: 'O God, return to so-and-so his she-camel.'
Muhammad said: I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and informed him, and he said, 'And he did it.'
I said, 'Yes.' He remained silent. I said, 'Should I repeat the prayer?' He said, 'No.'

key_terms.أَبُو بَصِيرٍ: Abu Basir, a companion of the Imams

ai.seo_question: Does making a supplication for a worldly matter while in prostration during prayer invalidate the prayer?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the permissibility of making personal supplications (du'a) for worldly needs, such as recovering a lost camel, while in the state of prostration (sujud) during prayer. Imam al-Sadiq’s initial silence followed by his confirmation that the prayer need not be repeated underscores the scholarly view that such interruptions do not break the validity of the prayer, reflecting the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding minor distractions during worship.
